div.head: Manuscripts
div.p: A manuscript is described once, in an msDesc: in the source description of a file that transcribes a text from it (), or as a record in a listBibl (). The description is TEI's own, restricted to what the application holds of a manuscript: the manuscript, its codicological units, each unit's contents and physical description, its hands and decoration, the binding, and the history of each. It is modelled on the Bodleian Libraries' guidelines for their catalogues, whose descriptions the project converts into its own ().

The import makes the manuscript's record, its units, and an item for each text, joined to the work's record; it makes the relations a description states: where a unit was made, who owned the manuscript, which scribe a hand was. An export writes the same form. Everything in a description is full.

div.head: The description and the manuscript's identifier
div.p: A description holds the manuscript's identifier; its binding, in a physical description of its own; the history of the whole book, where its units were joined and who has owned it since; what is additional, its images, literature and sources; and its units, one at least, each with its contents, physical description and history. The Collectio 400 capitulorum's manuscript, Munich, Clm 4592, in short: the binding and the additional are left out, and of its three units, the one that holds the collection:

supportDesc.extent: ff. 120–207, of ff. II, 207, II' in all 240 160

div.p: The file gives the physical description of the whole book too, and repeats it in each unit; the leaves are wrapped in num, the places and the library have no records, the units are numbered 11, 22 and 33, and the items point to the works by key. The template manuscript-collection.xml holds the whole description. Here, as everywhere in this part, the example is revised to the guide's forms.

The identifier names the manuscript's country, region and town, and its library, each pointing to its record by ref; the library's fonds, where it has one, in collection, the shelfmark still written whole in idno typed shelfmark; the manuscript's ids in other catalogues, each an idno typed by the authority (); its other identifiers, each an altIdentifier typed former (a former shelfmark), siglum (an editor's siglum) or code (the short code that files of the manuscript carry, Mun-BSB-4592); and its conventional names, in msName, one per language. A made-up manuscript:

A description holds only the elements this part names, each in its place: the contents and the physical description on a unit; on the manuscript, a physical description of the binding alone; no unit inside a unit; in adminInfo, the record's history alone; terms in a binding. Its prose, beside every value, holds a small set, so that what it mentions stays readable: locus; persName, placeName and orgName with ref; title with ref; date; foreign; hi, for italics and the like; and ref. A bibliography inside it keeps the forms of Part IX. Not the diplomatic set of the Bodleian's catalogues (am, ex, supplied, damage, fw, figure, formula, verse): quoting the manuscript is what transcriptions do. A count of leaves is words, without num. Each of these is an error; a description without a unit is one too:

constraintSpec.desc: A manuscript's description has at least one codicological unit.

sch:rule.sch:assert: A manuscript's description has at least one codicological unit (msPart), with its own identifier: the unit holds the physical description, the date, the hands and the decoration.

constraintSpec.desc: Inside a description, only the profile's elements, in their places, and the prose's phrase-level elements.

div.head: Units
div.p: A unit (msPart) is a codicological unit: leaves made together, which the manuscript may have joined to others. Every description has one at least: a manuscript made in one go has one. A unit's identifier is an idno without a type, with its number or letter and its leaves (3, ff. 120–207); n gives its order. A unit holds its own contents, physical description and history; the manuscript holds only what belongs to the whole book: its binding, its history since its units were joined, and what is additional. A unit isn't divided into units: a unit made of smaller ones that were once a book of their own is described by its parts, each a unit of the manuscript, with that history in each.

constraintSpec.desc: Every unit is dated, or said undated.

sch:assert.test: tei:history/tei:origin/tei:origDate[@when or @notBefore or @notAfter or @from or @to or @type = 'undated']

sch:rule.sch:assert: A unit is dated, in its origin's origDate with its bounds, or said undated (origDate type="undated").

div.head: Contents
div.p: A unit's contents (msContents) are its items, each a text in it (msItem): its folios, by locus with from and to, or locusGrp for leaves apart; its author and its title, each pointing to its record by ref, the title to the work; the manuscript's own words, rubric, incipit, explicit, finalRubric and colophon; its languages, textLang; and notes. An item's parts are items inside it: a collection's register and prefaces, a text copied within another. Contents not listed one by one are said in summary. An item that a file transcribes names its transcription by corresp: the file's code, as source notes name documents (), or, in exports, the transcription's permalink; each file's description can point to every transcription of the manuscript. An item's category is its work's, not the item's. In Clm 4592, the Constitutum Silvestri is excerpted inside the collection:

The file lists the excerpts as two more items of the unit, one with the author and one without, with escaped italics in their notes. An item without its folios is reported, since sources often give none:

sch:rule.sch:assert: An item gives its folios, by locus, or locusGrp for leaves apart, where its source gives them.

div.head: The physical description
div.p: A unit's physical description (physDesc) may begin with paragraphs, then holds its parts, each in prose with its values in attributes: the object (objectDesc), its form in form (codex, roll, …); its support (supportDesc), the material in material (perg, chart, …), described in support, with the extent in words and the leaves' dimensions, their unit always given, foliation, collation and condition; its layout (layoutDesc), each layout with its columns, ruledLines and writtenLines; then its hands, decoration and additions. A unit's extent may say what the whole book counts. Forms and materials come from vocabularies that grow: a term outside the guide's seeds is reported, to be checked or added to the application's vocabulary ( lists the seeds). Clm 4592's second unit:
The file gives the material only in words; the vocabulary's perg says it for the application. Dimensions without their unit are an error, and a form or a material outside the seeds is reported:

constraintSpec.desc: An object's form is one of the vocabulary's seeds, or a new term of it.

sch:rule.sch:assert: The form isn't among the vocabulary's seeds: check its spelling, or add it to the application's vocabulary.

div.head: Hands
div.p: A unit's hands are its handDesc's handNotes, one per hand, each with an xml:id, its script and its execution from vocabularies (script, execution, which TEI lacks and the guide adds, as the Bodleian's guidelines do), its share of the unit (scope: sole, major or minor), its folios, and prose. The hands are counted from their notes. A scribe is named in the prose by persName with ref, and the hand is the scribe's by a relation (), which can carry its certainty and evidence. A change in the text, an add, a del or a subst, points to the hand that made it by hand (); a hand pointed to in the file is described there. A made-up unit with two hands, a correction by the second, and the main hand's scribe:

handDesc.handNote: ff. 1r–40v: the main hand, perhaps Exemplus, whose name stands at the foot of f. 40v.
Corrections between the lines, in a browner ink.

div.p: A hand pointed to that the file doesn't describe is an error, and a script or an execution outside the seeds is reported:

constraintSpec.desc: A hand's script is one of the vocabulary's seeds, or a new term of it.

sch:rule.sch:assert: The script isn't among the vocabulary's seeds: check its spelling, or add it to the application's vocabulary.

constraintSpec.desc: A hand's execution is one of the vocabulary's seeds, or a new term of it.

sch:rule.sch:assert: The execution isn't among the vocabulary's seeds: check its spelling, or add it to the application's vocabulary.

constraintSpec.desc: A hand pointed to in the file is described there.

sch:rule.sch:assert: @hand points to a hand the file describes, a handNote with that xml:id ().

div.head: Decoration
div.p: A unit's decoration is its decoDesc's decoNotes, each of a kind, in type from the vocabulary of decoration (colInit for coloured initials, rubrication, miniature, …), with its folios and prose. A made-up unit:

decoDesc.decoNote: ff. 1r–40v: red and green initials at the chapters.

div.p: A kind outside the seeds is reported:

constraintSpec.desc: A decoration's type is one of the vocabulary's seeds, or a new term of it.

sch:rule.sch:assert: The decoration isn't among the vocabulary's seeds: check its spelling, or add it to the application's vocabulary.

valItem.desc: scenes at the foot of the page
coloured initials, not decorated or flourished
plain initials, in the ink of the text

div.head: The binding
div.p: The binding is the manuscript's, in its own physical description, which holds nothing else: a bindingDesc with a binding, described in paragraphs. Oxford encoding guide: "The standard dating attributes should be used on the binding element if information about the date of the binding is available." Its bounds go on binding, in the one form of dates (), and where they aren't known, contemporary says whether it is the manuscript's first binding: true, false, or unknown where nothing is known. The binding's materials and techniques are terms in its prose, each pointing by ref to its concept in Ligatus's Language of Bindings; its dimensions, with depth beside height and width, stand in its prose too. An earlier binding of one unit, before it was joined to the others, is said in a paragraph of the unit's physical description. A made-up binding:

binding.p: Calfskin over wooden boards, blind-tooled; two clasps, lost. 250 175 60

div.p: A binding neither dated nor said contemporary is an error, and so is a value of contemporary outside the three:

constraintSpec.desc: A binding is dated, or says whether it is contemporary.

sch:rule.sch:assert: A binding is dated by its bounds, or says whether it is contemporary with the manuscript (@contemporary: true, false, or unknown where nothing is known).

valItem.desc: the binding is contemporary with the manuscript
whether it is contemporary isn't known

div.head: History
div.p: A unit's history (history) is its origin and its owners; the manuscript's, the owners of the whole book since its units were joined, and where it was assembled. The origin (origin) holds the unit's date, origDate, in the one form of dates, its calendar named (), and its place, origPlace, pointing to the place's record by ref; the import makes the relation origin from them. Each owner is a provenance, or an acquisition for the library that holds the manuscript now, with its dates and the owner named inside by persName, orgName or placeName with ref, since TEI gives neither a pointer of its own; the import makes the relation ownedBy. Oxford encoding guide: "where possible each provenance event should occur in its own provenance element, which should have relevant dating attributes (when, notBefore, etc.)." Clm 4592's third unit was made at Salzburg in the second quarter of the ninth century:
A made-up owner, with the years of its ownership:

egXML.provenance: Owned by the cathedral of Exemplum, whose ex libris stands on f. 1r.

div.p: An origDate has no type but undated ():

valItem.desc: the unit is undated: no bounds, and the source's words if it has any

div.head: Images, literature, sources
div.p: What a description adds about the manuscript goes in the manuscript's additional: the description's own sources, in adminInfo's recordHist, each a bibl typed source in source, as every record names its own (); the manuscript's images, in surrogates, each IIIF manifest a ref typed iiif, its address in target and its provider in its words, which the application shows the pages from (a page break's canvas is the page break's, ); and the literature on it, in listBibl, in the forms of Part IX. div.head: The Bodleian's descriptions
div.p: The Bodleian Libraries' catalogues, and others written in their form, describe manuscripts in TEI with a schema of their own, which this part's description is modelled on. Their descriptions are an import format: the project converts them into its own form, with a converter outside this package. They needn't pass this guide's schema; before they are converted, they are checked against their own, at the commit the package pins:

The table in says what the conversion does with each element and attribute of the Bodleian's description: keeps it, moves it, makes a record or a relation of it, or drops it, and why. Of the project's coded files, 38 carry a description in the Bodleian's form, written before this guide; the corrections bring them to the guide's form.
